Bug_Details:
Classes that override equals should also override hashCode. The contract for Object.hashCode states that if two objects are equal, then
calling the hashCode() method on each of the two objects must produce the same
result. Implementing equals() but not hashCode() causes broken behaviour
when trying to store the object in a collection. See Effective Java 3rd Edition §11 for more information and a
discussion of how to correctly implement hashCode().
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by overriding the equals() method but not the hashCode() method. This violates the contract between equals() and hashCode(), causing unexpected behavior when objects are stored in collections.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug() method, which creates two instances of EqualsHashCodeExample with the same id and name. Since the hashCode() method is not overridden, the hash codes of the two instances are different, leading to a set size of 2 instead of 1 when they are added to a HashSet.
